children: Our Bureau New Delhi: Home services platform Urban Company has reported a quarterly net loss of 183 crore, weighed down by higher spending to compete in the instant house-help segment. The company said its InstaHelp business would continue to incur elevated losses for several quarters.

For the September quarter, the company's net loss was more than three times the Rs 59 crore loss recorded a year ago, according to the results declared on Friday. Gurgaon-based Urban Company competes with Nexus Venture Partners-backed Snabbit and General Catalyst-backed Pronto in the instant househelp segment.

Urban Company's operating revenue during the quarter stood at 537 crore, up by 41% from a year ago. The company's board, on October 16, also approved a plan to raise 2,500 crore. Urban Company had raised 472 crore through a public offering of shares in September 2025.

At the post-earnings analyst call, cofounder and chief executive officer Abhiraj Singh Bhal said InstaHelp's losses will remain elevated for many quarters to come. "We are building for scale, not near-term profits," he said, adding that from the third quarter of FY28, its core business profits will fund InstaHelp losses. On the proposed fundraise, Bhal said, "Should the competitive intensity in InstaHelp rise, we have both the balance sheet and the intent to respond in full."

title: Urban Company's Q2 Loss Triples to 183 crore on InstaHelp Biz Burn
